correctness.rationale: Open-neighborhood locating domination on the 18-vertex cubic Pappus affine-incidence graph: each outside vertex needs a distinct nonempty selected-neighbor trace. The crossing-edge inequality excludes |S|<=5 and forces an independent 3-point/3-line minimum set at |S|=6. The finite-field parametrization S_(a,b,c) (a=1,2; b,c in F3) exhausts exactly 18 optima; the explicit opposite-a incidence bijection yields the original Pappus graph from intersection-four edges. Direct independent subset enumeration gave 0,18,540,4869 admissible sets of cardinalities 5,6,7,8; optimum intersection histogram {0:18,1:54,2:54,4:27}. Independently constructed size<=8 reconfiguration transitions and exact BFS shortest paths verified all 153 optimum pairs have distance |S triangle T|. At capacity7 optima have no common 7-element superset (maximum mutual intersection 4), so each is isolated from other optima. The calculation is exhaustive for this finite graph; no assertion for a larger family or for connectivity of all size<=8 states.

value.rationale: The complete optimizer family, its unexpectedly self-isomorphic intersection graph, and the sharp two-spare-vertex reconfiguration threshold give a natural structural and transition classification on a classical incidence graph. The results are substantially stronger than a routine domination-number calculation; the exact Hamming-geodesic distances would support related optimal-code reconfiguration comparisons.
